title: Debating the New Hybrid Work Policy
script: Ilham: [frustrated] Citra, did you see the new policy? Management wants everyone back in the office four days a week starting next month.
Citra: [surprised] Four days? I thought the whole point of hybrid work was flexibility. This feels like a step backward to me.
Ilham: [agreeing] Exactly my reaction. If productivity hasn't actually dropped, then what's really driving this decision?
Citra: [thoughtful] I heard it's partly about collaboration. Apparently, some managers feel that spontaneous conversations happen less often when everyone works remotely.
Ilham: [skeptical] Maybe, although I've had plenty of useful conversations over video calls too. It's not as though remote work eliminates collaboration entirely.
Citra: [considering] That's true for some teams, however I'll admit our newer employees have struggled a bit without in-person guidance.
Ilham: [conceding] Okay, that's a fair point. Even though I personally prefer working from home, I understand that newer staff might need more direct support.
Citra: [thoughtful] What if the policy applied differently depending on experience, rather than forcing everyone into the exact same schedule?
Ilham: [interested] That actually sounds reasonable. Senior employees who've proven they work well remotely shouldn't necessarily be treated the same as brand-new hires.
Citra: [nodding] Right, and despite understanding the reasoning behind more office time, four days still feels excessive compared to two or three.
Ilham: [determined] Should we raise this suggestion at Friday's meeting, instead of simply accepting the policy without any discussion at all?
Citra: [encouraging] Definitely. If we present it calmly, with reasons rather than complaints, management is more likely to actually consider it.
Ilham: [thoughtful] I'll gather some data on our team's output over the past year, so the argument isn't based purely on personal preference.
Citra: [pleased] Good idea. Numbers tend to persuade decision-makers far more effectively than frustration alone, no matter how justified that frustration feels.
Ilham: [warmly] Agreed. Let's meet tomorrow morning to prepare properly, so we're not improvising our argument in front of the whole department.
Citra: [smiling] Sounds good. Honestly, I feel better already, just knowing we're doing something instead of quietly complaining to each other.
